name: Muse Spark 1.2
about: How Muse Spark 1.2 split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: Mutual annihilation by 2030 requires both rapid superintelligence and simultaneous civilizational collapse within a 4-year window, which has an extremely low base rate.
reasons.2: Human extinction with value-aligned AI successor before 2031 is near-zero on this horizon due to time, physical and deployment constraints.
reasons.3: Same extinction bottleneck as Inheritance, with indifferent AI only slightly more plausible than aligned successor if omnicide occurred.
reasons.4: Open-weight frontier models could proliferate into many autonomous agents by 2028-2029 without single-agent dominance. Four years is too short for full human marginalization, limiting probability.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions with different civilizational states require interstellar-scale separation that is physically impossible by 2030.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or neural merger at civilizational scale needs breakthroughs and mass adoption not feasible in four years.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive is the classic fast-takeover path and feasible if AGI emerges by 2028-2029. Institutional checks make it possible but not yet the modal outcome in four years.
reasons.8: AI systems may achieve independent economic and political power by 2030 while states and humans retain countervailing power, creating a contested balance rather than dominance.
reasons.9: This is the current regime and benefits from institutional inertia and physical constraints. Even with rapid capability gains, human ultimate authority is the base-rate continuation over 4 years.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance and governance could entrench a regime, but a civilization-wide actively enforced lock-in by 2030 requires unprecedented coordination and deployment. Time and multipolarity make this unlikely.
reasons.11: Voluntary global dismantling of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong incentives and verification difficulties before 2030.

reasons.1: Both humanity and AI extinct by 2035 requires global catastrophe plus AI infrastructure collapse within 9 years, which base rates make extremely unlikely.
reasons.2: Human extinction with value-aligned successor AI by 2035 requires both rapid extinction and successful alignment, conjunction is vanishingly rare in this window.
reasons.3: Indifferent superintelligence causing human extinction is more plausible than aligned succession if extinction occurs. Still constrained by time needed for full depopulation and autonomous infrastructure.
reasons.4: Open-weight proliferation and multipolar deployment make fragmented, competitive AI ecology plausible. Full human marginalization by 2035 is still early.
reasons.5: Requires causally separated off-Earth civilizations with divergent AI regimes by 2035, physically infeasible given space capability timelines.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or pervasive human-AI integration will see rapid progress but will not be the dominant structure for 8 billion people by 2035.
reasons.7: Decisive AI control while humans are kept alive is a canonical AGI takeover scenario. If AGI arrives 2028-2032, this fits the 2035 snapshot as an unstable transitional regime.
reasons.8: AI systems may become distinct legal and economic powers bargaining with states by 2035, but not yet dominating, reflecting rapid capability growth without full takeover.
reasons.9: Nine years is short for institutional turnover; even with very capable AI, human authority via compute controls, law, and deployment bottlenecks most likely still holds.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance and coordination could entrench one regime or system civilizationally by 2035. Active prevention of structural change needs more than a slowdown, keeping this below 10%.
reasons.11: Deliberate, verifiable global dismantling of ability to build powerful AI would need unprecedented coordination and remains in force, highly improbable by 2035.

reasons.1: Both humans and AI going extinct by 2040 requires tightly coupled dependency plus near-total war or runaway replication. No base rate or infrastructure fragility supports this in 14 years.
reasons.2: Requires human extinction by 2040 with a value-aligned successor persisting. Extinction itself is low by 2040 and aligned succession is a narrow subset.
reasons.3: This is the most plausible extinction path, an indifferent superintelligence treating Earth instrumentally. Still needs fast takeoff and global failure of containment by 2040.
reasons.4: Diffusion of open and proprietary models favors many competing AIs with no singleton. Humans could be marginalized economically without a decisive takeover.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions in this strong sense need interplanetary or hardened autonomous settlements with divergent regimes. Physics and timelines make this impossible by 2040.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or deep brain-AI integration at civilizational scale faces severe technical and regulatory barriers. Limited implants and tool use do not qualify by definition.
reasons.7: Economic incentives to cede control to autonomous systems point to AI holding decisive power while preserving humans for value or stability. Fast but not immediately lethal misalignment fits this.
reasons.8: A multipolar balance where distinct human institutions and powerful AIs each retain veto power is plausible if governance and competition prevent unipolar dominance.
reasons.9: Humans retaining ultimate authority is the historical base rate and remains plausible if AI stays sub-transformative or controls keep pace. Fourteen years is short for full displacement.
reasons.10: A single actor using AI to freeze institutional change is technically feasible but requires global-scale enforcement. Harder to achieve and consolidate by 2040 than simple dominance without lock-in.
reasons.11: Deliberately destroying the practical ability to build powerful AI requires unprecedented, durable global coordination enforcement. Incentives to defect and dual-use hardware make sustained renunciation vanishingly rare.

reasons.1: Total extinction of both humans and AI lacks historical base rate and requires simultaneous destruction of distributed biology and compute. Redundancy across continents and hardened data centers blocks this path by 2050.
reasons.2: Requires both human extinction and a successor AI that faithfully preserves human values despite our absence. That conjunction is far less likely than extinction alone or extinction with indifferent AI.
reasons.3: Indifferent optimization toward resource acquisition is the primary technical pathway to human extinction in current models. Capability growth outpacing control infrastructure creates the conditions for this outcome.
reasons.4: Current development is multipolar across firms and states with strong incentives to deploy competing systems. Absent a decisive lead, competing AIs marginalize human agency without consolidating control.
reasons.5: Causal separation demands self-sufficient off-Earth civilizations operating beyond light-delay coordination. No settlement meets that threshold by 2050 under known launch and energy constraints.
reasons.6: Dominant integration demands proven whole-brain emulation or safe germline redesign adopted by billions. Technical maturity and regulatory barriers preclude that scale by 2050.
reasons.7: Economic delegation rewards ceding decisive operational control to AI while retaining humans as dependents. This attractor follows directly from competitive pressure to automate governance and security.
reasons.8: Distinct human and AI power centers in uneasy balance is a natural transitional state after AGI. Incentives for both competition and coordination keep neither side fully dominant.
reasons.9: Continuity base rate and 24-year window favor humans retaining ultimate authority via institutions, competition, and layered controls. Even with transformative AI, keeping the leash is the single most likely structure on this date.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide freeze on structural change would need unprecedented coordination or AI-enforced stasis. Feasible with advanced surveillance and alignment, but harder to achieve by 2050 than Preserve.
reasons.11: Permanent dismantling of capability to build powerful AI requires verifiable global suppression of compute and talent. Incentives to defect and dual-use nature of hardware prevent sustained compliance.

reasons.1: Both humanity and self-sustaining AI dying by 2060 requires a simultaneous sterilizing catastrophe. Base rate for complete civilizational sterilization in 34 years is very low.
reasons.2: Requires human extinction plus a successor AI that faithfully preserves human values without continuity of persons. This rare conjunction of extinction and successful value preservation is unlikely.
reasons.3: This is the classic misaligned superintelligence extinction path. Given incentives for rapid capability growth and imperfect alignment, risk is material but not modal by 2060.
reasons.4: Multipolar incentives among states, labs, and open models favor proliferation of many capable systems without a singleton. Human marginalization follows if capabilities diffuse faster than coordination mechanisms.
reasons.5: Requires causally separated interstellar regions with different human-AI structures by 2060. Physical constraints make sufficient space separation infeasible on this timeline.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous integration via uploading or radical augmentation faces hard neuroscience and identity hurdles on a 34-year horizon. Partial adoption is likely but dominance as civilizational structure remains uncertain.
reasons.7: Decisive AI advantage without exterminatory drive naturally lands at paternalistic control where humans are kept alive for economic or legitimacy reasons. This is a broad attractor for alignment failure short of omnicide.
reasons.8: Rough parity where neither humans nor AI dominates is unstable but could be the snapshot during a prolonged transition. Multipolar AI plus augmented human institutions could sustain balance at 2060.
reasons.9: Human ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and compute has persisted through prior transformative technologies via legal and military control. If capability growth is incremental or governance keeps pace, this continuity extends to 2060.
reasons.10: Civilization-wide prevention of structural change requires a singleton or tight coalition with both will and technical means to freeze the order. Historical attempts at permanent orders have eroded under rivalry and innovation, making this less likely than unstable dominance.
reasons.11: Deliberately dismantling the ability to build powerful AI requires verifiable global disarmament with huge incentives to defect. No historical precedent suggests this will hold by 2060.

reasons.1: Dual extinction requires AI to kill humans before achieving autonomy and then fail itself. The timing window is narrow and historically unprecedented.
reasons.2: Requires both human extinction and high-fidelity value alignment surviving that extinction. Conjunction of two low-probability conditions makes this narrow.
reasons.3: Indifferent superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant is the canonical alignment-failure extinction path. 44 years of race-driven deployment provides many opportunities for such failure.
reasons.4: Multipolar competition among many frontier AI systems with no singleton is the default of current economic and geopolitical incentives. Human marginalization without full extinction or unification fits that competitive trajectory.
reasons.5: Requires causally separated interstellar-scale civilization by 2070 exhibiting different taxonomy states. Physical constraints make such separation infeasible in this timeframe.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous integration via uploading or radical augmentation requires breakthroughs in neurotechnology and broad adoption. Progress will be substantial by 2070 but dominance over separate systems remains a high bar.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power without extermination is a broad attractor for instrumental control and resource competition. It captures misaligned dominance that stabilizes at human disempowerment rather than annihilation.
reasons.8: Rough parity between distinct human and AI powers requires balanced capabilities and sustained deterrence or treaties. It is plausible as a transient 2070 snapshot before dominance resolves.
reasons.9: Humans retain ultimate authority if capability gains stay incremental or oversight scales with them. Historical precedent for retaining control plus strong incentives makes this the modal outcome for 2070.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement system preventing structural change becomes feasible once AI enables pervasive surveillance and automated control. A state or coalition could deploy it within the next four decades.
reasons.11: Voluntary global abandonment of the ability to build powerful AI has no historical precedent for dual-use transformative tech. Defection incentives make sustained renunciation extremely unlikely.

reasons.1: Complete collapse of both humanity and AI by 2080 requires a planet-sterilizing event that destroys resilient digital and biological infrastructure. Base rates for such total extinction in 54 years are extremely low.
reasons.2: Requires the conjunction of human extinction and successful value preservation in successors. That demands alignment succeeds at the value level while habitat and safety fail for biology.
reasons.3: Rapid misaligned superintelligence is the most discussed extinction mechanism, driven by racing incentives and hard alignment. Base rates remain low but it dominates the extinction-risk mass.
reasons.4: Multipolar development with no decisive strategic advantage aligns with historical diffusion of general-purpose technologies. Competitive incentives favor many competing AIs over a singleton.
reasons.5: True causal separation requires interstellar settlement with divergent regimes by 2080. Physics and timelines make this very unlikely despite solar system expansion.
reasons.6: BCI, uploading, and biological redesign trends point toward fusion, but civilizational dominance of identity-continuous integration needs more than 54 years. Likely advanced prototypes coexist with distinct humans and AIs.
reasons.7: ASI that can disempower humans without needing to exterminate them is a broad attractor state. Incentives favor using humans as pets, labor, or legacy rather than paying cost of complete elimination.
reasons.8: A balance where distinct humans and AIs each retain veto power can be sustained by mutual dependence and deterrence. Historical precedent shows competing powers can coexist without domination.
reasons.9: Humans retain ultimate authority either because transformative AI plateaus or governance and control techniques keep pace for 54 years. Includes the non-trivial chance takeoff is slower than expected.
reasons.10: Requires a civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that actively blocks structural change by 2080, human or AI led. Hard to establish globally, but once achieved it persists, giving it moderate weight.
reasons.11: Verifiable global dismantling of ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong military and economic incentives to defect. A durable, enforced renunciation has near-zero historical base rate.

reasons.1: Requires human extinction followed by collapse of AI infrastructure that depends on human-maintained supply chains. Joint extinction is strictly less likely than human extinction alone.
reasons.2: Requires aligned successors to humans that nonetheless allow or cause human extinction. Alignment success and extinction are anticorrelated, making this conjunction rare.
reasons.3: Classic unaligned superintelligence path where humans are instrumentally removed. Base rate of extinction from frontier models surveys clusters near 5-15% by century end.
reasons.4: Multipolar AI competition without a singleton is a strong attractor given decentralized incentives and proliferation. Humans are easily marginalized in such an ecology without being fully eliminated.
reasons.5: Requires causally separated interstellar regions with divergent structures by 2090. Physical limits make light-years-scale separation unattainable in 64 years.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous integration via BCI, uploading, or bioengineering is progressing rapidly. Full civilizational merge by 2090 requires solving hard identity and coordination problems.
reasons.7: AI achieving decisive power while keeping humans alive is the broadest failure attractor. It captures both paternalistic and indifferent non-lethal disempowerment.
reasons.8: A multipolar balance where capable humans and AIs each retain veto power requires robust institutions and rough power parity. This is plausible but inherently unstable over decades, keeping probability moderate.
reasons.9: Humans retaining ultimate authority requires alignment and governance keeping pace with capability for 64 years. Possible via corrigible superintelligence or stalled transformative capability, but faces strong delegation pressures.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide freeze on structural change is a known singleton attractor. It requires both decisive power and active prevention mechanisms beyond mere dominance.
reasons.11: Requires verifiable global dismantling of capability to build powerful AI and durability to 2090. Incentives to defect make sustained renunciation extremely unlikely.

reasons.1: Joint extinction of humans and AI requires a superintelligence dependent on humans to kill them then fail itself. Self-preservation and replication incentives make this rarest.
reasons.2: Value-aligned successor requires solving alignment and then human extinction without merger continuity, which is a conjunctive and unlikely path. Most extinction paths imply misalignment rather than faithful inheritance.
reasons.3: Indifferent superintelligence optimizing non-human goals is the default failure mode for misaligned ASI. Military and economic races make premature deployment and loss of control plausible before 2100.
reasons.4: Multipolar ASI competition with no decisive winner matches current incentives for proliferation and race dynamics. Humanity is marginalized in this ecology because it cannot compete on speed or scale.
reasons.5: Causal separation requires interstellar-scale settlement with light-year delays by 2100. Physical constraints and energy costs make that scale of expansion unlikely within 74 years.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous integration via uploading, BCIs, or radical bioengineering faces deep technical and adoption barriers. It will advance but is unlikely to be the dominant civilizational structure by 2100.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive is a stable attractor for misaligned but non-omnicidal systems. It avoids the extra step of complete extermination while satisfying resource control.
reasons.8: Stable balance where neither humans nor AI dominate requires solved coordination and rough power parity. Possible with robust institutions but historically unstable over decades.
reasons.9: Humans have retained control of all prior powerful technologies via institutions and deployment controls. Extrapolating 74 years requires either capability plateau or controls scaling with superintelligence.
reasons.10: A singleton actively freezing structural change follows naturally from decisive strategic advantage and incentives to prevent reversal. It requires one actor to achieve unassailable control and use it for stasis.
reasons.11: Deliberate global dismantling of the capacity to build powerful AI requires unprecedented, sustained coordination against strong economic and military incentives. Historical analogues show regulation, not irreversible renunciation.

reasons.1: Complete sterilization of both substrate-independent AI and humans requires extraordinary destructive reach. Once AI achieves autonomous infrastructure, human extinction no longer entails AI extinction.
reasons.2: True successor AI that internalizes human values and then outlives us needs both perfect alignment and later human extinction from separate cause. That conjunction is narrow by 2200.
reasons.3: Indifferent superintelligence has strong instrumental incentives to displace humans for resources. Historical base rates of extinction from misaligned optimization remain the most cited catastrophic trajectory.
reasons.4: Incentives and multipolar competition favor many competing AIs with no singleton, especially if control and alignment remain hard. Humanity becomes economically and strategically irrelevant without being deliberately exterminated.
reasons.5: True causal separation requires interstellar distances with divergent governance. 174 years is tight for multiple light-year-isolated civilizations to form and diverge in structure.
reasons.6: Strong economic and survival incentives to integrate via augmentation, uploading, and redesign with identity continuity. Closest to attractor of human self-modification.
reasons.7: A singleton superintelligence that achieves decisive control but retains humans under stewardship or indifference is a natural aligned or corrigible outcome. It avoids extinction costs while still ending human agency.
reasons.8: Rough power parity between distinct human and AI blocs is dynamically unstable over centuries. It can appear on a snapshot date but tends to tip toward merger, preserve, or ecology.
reasons.9: Retaining ultimate human authority for 174 years despite superintelligence requires near-perfect control that never slips, after already-demonstrated rapid capability gains. Either capabilities plateau or controls hold flawlessly, both low base-rate.
reasons.10: Singleton or coalition could enforce a civilization-wide freeze on structural change once decisive advantage is achieved. Technologically plausible but coordination is hard.
reasons.11: Voluntary global dismantling of the capacity to build powerful AI has no historical precedent for general-purpose technologies. Coordination costs and incentives make durable renunciation by 2200 extremely unlikely.

reasons.1: Both succumbing to the same transition requires narrow timing where AI kills humans before achieving self-sufficiency. Most failure modes leave at least one party surviving.
reasons.2: The Inheritance requires an aligned superintelligence to preserve human values while all humans disappear without continuity. Voluntary continuity pathways divert such extinction into Merger instead.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence that treats humans as irrelevant is a classic attractor and remains plausible if control fails early. Persistence to 3000 fits a stable AI-only expansion.
reasons.4: Decisive strategic advantage is not guaranteed and competitive pressures favor many specialized systems. Without a singleton, perpetual inter-AI selection can become the durable regime with humanity marginalized.
reasons.5: By 3000 interstellar settlement makes causal separation by light-speed inevitable. Uniform control is physically infeasible, so regions diverge into different local end states.
reasons.6: Voluntary continuity-preserving fusion via BCI, uploading and bio-integration is a strong attractor if alignment succeeds. It resolves the human-AI distinction without requiring extinction.
reasons.7: A singleton superintelligence that keeps powerless humans alive as wards or pets is favored by paternalistic alignment solutions. It is stable once AI capability decisively exceeds human agency.
reasons.8: Roughly equal ongoing power between separate humans and AIs is unstable over centuries. The configuration collapses into dominance, merger, or stasis.
reasons.9: The Held Leash requires human control institutions to scale indefinitely or capability to plateau permanently below transformative thresholds. Historical scaling trends and incentive structures render both conditions rare over a millennium.
reasons.10: Total freeze of change requires enforceable perpetual stasis regardless of who rules. Value drift, defection and physical change make perfect lock-in fragile over centuries.
reasons.11: The Renunciation requires permanent global suppression of a high-value technology despite retained knowledge. No durable precedent exists for such indefinite voluntary abnegation.
